subject: maths
title: Decimals: Thousandths, Comparing and Number Lines
seo_title: Year 5 Decimals Worksheets: Thousandths, Compare, Order and Number Lines (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Interpret, compare and order numbers with more than 2 decimal places, including numbers greater than one, using place value understanding; represent these on a number line
meta_desc: Free Year 5 decimals worksheets for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M5N01): place value to thousandths, decimals as fractions and mixed numerals, comparing and ordering decimals, and number lines. 100 maths questions with an answer key, good NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Compare decimals by place value, not by length: 0.5 = 0.500 > 0.45 > 0.405.
key_sub: Three decimal places are thousandths: 0.045 = 45/1000. On a number line, work out what one space is worth before you count.
body_html:
Place value to thousandths

Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. After the decimal point come tenths, hundredths and thousandths. 1 hundredth split into 10 equal parts makes 10 thousandths.

Decimals as fractions and mixed numerals

The number of decimal places tells you the denominator: one place is tenths, two places are hundredths, three places are thousandths. A number greater than one becomes a mixed numeral.

DecimalFractionSaid as
0.77107 tenths
0.717110071 hundredths
0.04545100045 thousandths
2.32 3102 and 3 tenths
2.092 91002 and 9 hundredths

Comparing and ordering

Compare the whole numbers first. Then give the numbers the same number of decimal places by adding zeros at the end, and compare the digits from the left: tenths, hundredths, thousandths.

Example 1

Order 0.5, 0.45 and 0.405 from smallest to greatest.

Write 0.500, 0.450 and 0.405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths.

Answer: 0.405, 0.45, 0.5

Example 2

Order 1.6, 1.06, 0.96 and 1.059 from smallest to greatest.

0.96 has 0 ones, so it is the smallest. Then 1.600, 1.060 and 1.059.

Answer: 0.96, 1.059, 1.06, 1.6

Decimals on a number line

First work out what one space is worth: the difference between two labels ÷ the number of spaces. Then count the spaces from a labelled number.

Example 3

A number line goes from 0.4 to 0.5 in 5 equal spaces. What is the second tick after 0.4?

0.1 ÷ 5 = 0.02, so each space is 0.02. Two spaces: 0.42, 0.44.

Answer: 0.44

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.405 > 0.5 because it is longerUse the same places: 0.405 < 0.500
0.045 = 45100Three places means thousandths: 451000
2.3 = 2 3100One place means tenths: 2.3 = 2 310
Every space on a number line is 0.1Work out each space first: 5 spaces from 0.4 to 0.5 are 0.02 each
A smaller race time losesIn a race, the smallest time is the fastest

faq.q: What do Year 5 students learn about decimals in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 5 (AC9M5N01) students interpret, compare and order decimals with more than 2 decimal places, including numbers greater than one, using place value, and show them on a number line.

faq.q: How do you compare decimals with different numbers of decimal places?
faq.a: Compare the whole numbers first, then add zeros at the end so the decimals have the same number of places and compare from the left. 0.5 = 0.500 and 0.45 = 0.450, so 0.5 is greater even though 0.45 has more digits.

faq.q: How do you write a decimal as a fraction or a mixed numeral?
faq.a: Count the decimal places: one place is tenths, two are hundredths and three are thousandths. So 0.045 = 45/1000 and 2.3 = 2 3/10.

faq.q: How do you read decimals on a number line?
faq.a: Find what one space is worth by dividing the gap between two labels by the number of spaces, then count on from a label. From 2.1 to 2.11 in 10 spaces, each space is 0.001.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 3.407?
items.e: The red 7 is the third digit after the decimal point, in the thousandths column. Its value is 7 thousandths = 0.007. The 0 holds the hundredths place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 5.064?
items.e: The red 6 is the second digit after the decimal point, in the hundredths column. Its value is 6 hundredths = 0.06.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 12.583?
items.e: The red 5 is the first digit after the decimal point, in the tenths column. Its value is 5 tenths = 0.5.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 6.192?
items.e: 6 . 1 9 2: the 9 is the second digit after the point, in the hundredths place. It is worth 9 hundredths = 0.09.

items.q: In 8.346, which digit is in the hundredths place?
items.e: After the point the places are tenths (3), hundredths (4) and thousandths (6). So the hundredths digit is 4.

items.q: In which place is the digit 4 in 0.024?
items.e: 0 . 0 2 4: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. The 4 is in the thousandths place.

items.q: In 15.208, which digit is in the thousandths place?
items.e: After the point: tenths 2, hundredths 0, thousandths 8. The thousandths digit is 8.

items.q: Which number is equal to 0.6?
items.e: A 0 at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 0.6 = 0.60 = 0.600. 0.06 and 0.006 have the 6 in a different place.

items.q: Write 3 ones, 5 hundredths and 2 thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: There are 0 tenths, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 3 . 0 5 2 = 3.052. 3.52 would have 5 tenths.
There are no tenths, so the tenths digit is 0: 7 . 0 8 5 = 7.085. 7.85 forgets the 0 that holds the tenths place.
4 ones, 6 tenths, 3 hundredths and 9 thousandths: 4 . 6 3 9 = 4.639.

items.q: Which shows 2.716 in expanded form?
items.e: 2 ones, 7 tenths, 1 hundredth and 6 thousandths: 2 + 0.7 + 0.01 + 0.006.

items.q: 1 hundredth is split into 10 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: A hundredth divided by 10 is a thousandth: 11000 = 0.001. 1 whole = 10 tenths = 100 hundredths = 1000 thousandths.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 1 hundredth?
items.e: 1 hundredth = 0.01 = 0.010. That is 10 thousandths.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0.3?
items.e: 1 tenth = 100 thousandths, so 3 tenths = 300 thousandths. 0.3 = 0.300.

items.q: In 5.55, the 5 in the tenths place is worth how many times the 5 in the hundredths place?
items.e: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. 0.5 = 10 × 0.05. So the answer is 10.

items.q: What number is 0.001 more than 4.209?
items.e: 9 thousandths + 1 thousandth = 10 thousandths = 1 hundredth. So 4.209 + 0.001 = 4.210 = 4.21. 4.219 adds 1 hundredth, not 1 thousandth.

items.q: What number is 0.01 more than 2.396?
items.e: Add 1 hundredth: 9 hundredths + 1 hundredth = 10 hundredths = 1 tenth. So 2.396 + 0.01 = 2.406. 2.397 adds only 1 thousandth.

items.q: What number is 0.1 less than 6.05?
items.e: Take away 1 tenth. 6.05 has 0 tenths, so regroup 1 one as 10 tenths: 6.05 − 0.1 = 5.95. 6.04 takes away 1 hundredth.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 1, 5 once to make the greatest number with 1 digit before the decimal point and 3 digits after it.
items.e: Put the largest digit in the ones place, then the next largest in the tenths, hundredths and thousandths: 8.531. 1.358 is the smallest number.

sets.title: Decimals as fractions and mixed numerals

items.q: Write 0.3 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.3 has one decimal place, so the 3 is in the tenths place: 3 tenths = 310.

items.q: Write 0.71 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.71 has two decimal places, so it is hundredths: 71 hundredths = 71100. 7110 would be 7.1.

items.q: Write 0.09 as a fraction.
items.e: Two decimal places means hundredths. The tenths digit is 0, so 0.09 = 9 hundredths = 9100.

items.q: Write 29100 as a decimal.
items.e: 29 hundredths: the last digit goes in the second place after the point. 29100 = 0.29.

items.q: Write 71000 as a decimal.
items.e: 7 thousandths: the 7 goes in the third place after the point. Write 0s in the tenths and hundredths places: 0.007.

items.q: Write 0.045 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.045 has three decimal places, so it is thousandths: 45 thousandths = 451000. 45100 would be 0.45.

items.q: Write 0.007 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.007 has three decimal places, so the 7 is in the thousandths place: 71000. 7100 would be 0.07.

items.q: Write 2.3 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 2 wholes, then 0.3 = 3 tenths. So 2.3 = 2 310. 2 3100 would be 2.03.

items.q: Write 3 710 as a decimal.
items.e: 3 wholes and 7 tenths. Tenths are the first place after the point: 3.7.

items.q: Write 2.09 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 2 wholes, then 0.09 = 9 hundredths. So 2.09 = 2 9100. 2 910 would be 2.9.

items.q: Write 5 6100 as a decimal.
items.e: 5 wholes and 6 hundredths. The 6 must be in the second place, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 5.06.

items.q: Write 0.453 as a fraction.
items.e: Three decimal places means thousandths: 0.453 = 453 thousandths = 4531000. 31000 is only the last digit.

items.q: Write 631000 as a decimal.
items.e: 63 thousandths = 6 hundredths and 3 thousandths. The last digit must be in the third place: 0.063. 0.63 would be 63 hundredths.

items.q: Write 4.125 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 4 wholes, then 0.125 has three decimal places = 125 thousandths. So 4.125 = 4 1251000. Do not forget the 4 wholes.

items.q: Write 12 481000 as a decimal.
items.e: 12 wholes and 48 thousandths. The last digit must be in the third place: 12.048. 12.48 would be 12 and 48 hundredths.

items.q: 0.35 = 35100 = ?1000
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 10: 35100 = 3501000. So the missing number is 350. 0.35 = 0.350.

items.q: 610 + 4100 + 91000 = ?
items.e: 6 tenths, 4 hundredths and 9 thousandths: 0 . 6 4 9 = 0.649.

items.q: Write two and four hundred and five thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: 2 wholes and 405 thousandths. Thousandths fill three places after the point: 2.405. 2.45 leaves out the 0 in the hundredths place.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to 0.5?
items.e: 510 = 50100 = 5001000 = 0.5. 0.05 is only 5 hundredths.

items.q: How many hundredths are there in 3.06?
items.e: 3 wholes = 300 hundredths, and 0.06 = 6 hundredths. 300 + 6 = 306 hundredths. So 3.06 = 306100.

items.q: Compare 0.5 and 0.45.
items.e: 0.5 = 0.50. Compare the tenths: 5 tenths > 4 tenths. So 0.5 > 0.45. More digits does not mean a bigger number.

items.q: Compare 0.38 and 0.4.
items.e: 0.4 = 0.40. Compare the tenths: 3 < 4. So 0.38 < 0.4.

items.q: Compare 2.07 and 2.070.
items.e: A 0 at the end does not change the value. 2.07 = 2.070, so 2.07 = 2.070.

items.q: Compare 0.009 and 0.09.
items.e: 0.09 = 0.090. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 9. So 0.009 < 0.09. 9 thousandths is less than 9 hundredths.

items.q: Compare 0.98 and 1.02.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 0 < 1. So 0.98 < 1.02. Any number less than 1 is smaller than any number greater than 1.

items.q: Compare 0.405 and 0.45.
items.e: Write both with 3 places: 0.405 and 0.450. The tenths are the same. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 5. So 0.405 < 0.45.

items.q: Compare 3.125 and 3.12.
items.e: 3.12 = 3.120. Ones, tenths and hundredths are the same. Compare the thousandths: 5 > 0. So 3.125 > 3.12.

items.q: Compare 1.9 and 1.899.
items.e: 1.9 = 1.900. The ones are the same. Compare the tenths: 9 > 8. So 1.9 > 1.899.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.700, 0.680, 0.699, 0.075. Compare the tenths first: only 0.7 has 7 tenths. So 0.7 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.205, 0.250, 0.300, 0.520. The smallest is 0.205, even though it has the most digits.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
0.5, 0.45, 0.405
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths. So 0.405, 0.45, 0.5.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare the ones first: 4.987 has only 4 ones. Then 5.100, 5.090, 5.099: 1 tenth beats 0 tenths. So 5.1 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is between 0.4 and 0.5?
items.e: 0.4 = 0.400 and 0.5 = 0.500. 0.408 is between them. 0.048 and 0.399 are less than 0.4, and 0.54 is more than 0.5.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
1.6, 1.06, 0.96, 1.059
items.e: 0.96 has 0 ones, so it is the smallest. Then write the rest with 3 places: 1.600, 1.060, 1.059. So 0.96, 1.059, 1.06, 1.6.

items.q:
Order from greatest to smallest:
3.2, 3.18, 3.205, 3.02
Which number is between 2.3 and 2.31?

Order from smallest to greatest:
0.6, 0.06, 0.606, 0.066
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.600, 0.060, 0.606, 0.066. Compare 600, 60, 606 and 66 thousandths. So 0.06, 0.066, 0.6, 0.606.

items.q:
Order from greatest to smallest:
10.5, 9.75, 10.05, 10.495
items.e: 9.75 is less than 10, so it is the smallest. Then 10.500, 10.495, 10.050. Greatest first: 10.5, 10.495, 10.05, 9.75.

items.q:
How many of these numbers are greater than 0.6?
0.59, 0.61, 0.596, 0.601

0.4□7 < 0.45
What is the greatest digit that can go in the box?
items.e: 0.45 = 0.450. With 4 in the box: 0.447 < 0.450. With 5: 0.457 > 0.450. So the greatest digit is 4.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: The line goes from 0 to 1 in 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 tenth (0.1). The dot is 7 spaces from 0: 0.7.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: The line goes from 0 to 0.1 in 10 equal spaces. 0.1 = 0.10, so each space is 1 hundredth (0.01). 6 spaces from 0: 0.06.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0.3 to 0.4 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. Count 8 spaces on from 0.30: 0.38.

items.q: Which point shows 2.07?
items.e: Each space is 0.1. 2.07 is less than 2.1, so it sits before the first tick: point A. Point C is 2.7.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 2.1 to 2.2 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. Count 4 spaces on from 2.10: 2.14.

items.q: How much is each space on this number line worth?
items.e: 0.7 − 0.6 = 0.1. Split 0.1 into 10 equal spaces: each space is 0.01 (1 hundredth).

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: There are only 5 spaces from 0 to 1, so each space is 0.2 (1 ÷ 5). The dot is 3 spaces along: 0.2, 0.4, 0.6. 0.3 counts the spaces as tenths.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 1 to 1.1 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. 9 spaces on from 1.00 is 1.09. 1.9 would be much further along, near 2.

items.q: Which point shows 0.35?
items.e: Each space is 0.01. 0.35 = 0.30 + 5 hundredths, so it is 5 spaces along: point C. Point A is 0.305, halfway between 0.30 and 0.31.

items.q: What number is halfway between 0.3 and 0.4?
items.e: 0.3 = 0.30 and 0.4 = 0.40. Halfway between 30 and 40 hundredths is 35 hundredths: 0.35.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: There are 4 spaces from 1 to 2, so each space is 0.25 (a quarter). The dot is 3 spaces along: 1.25, 1.5, 1.75.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: There are 5 spaces from 0.4 to 0.5, so each space is 0.1 ÷ 5 = 0.02. The dot is 2 spaces along: 0.42, 0.44. 0.42 counts each space as 0.01.

items.q: How much is each space on this number line worth?
items.e: 0.2 − 0 = 0.2 = 20 hundredths. There are 4 spaces, and 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Each space is 0.05. 0.02 assumes there are 10 spaces.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 2.1 to 2.11 there are 10 equal spaces. 2.11 − 2.10 = 0.01, so each space is 1 thousandth. Count 7 spaces on from 2.100: 2.107.

items.q: How much is each space on this number line worth?
items.e: 4.26 − 4.25 = 0.01. Split 0.01 into 10 equal spaces: each space is 0.001 (1 thousandth).

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0.45 to 0.46 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 thousandth. Count 2 spaces on from 0.450: 0.452.

items.q: Which point shows 1.508?
items.e: Each space is 0.01. 1.508 = 1.50 + 8 thousandths. 8 thousandths is less than 1 hundredth, so the point is inside the first space, close to 1.51: point A. Point C is 1.58.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 2.11 to 2.12 there are 10 spaces, so each space is 1 thousandth. The dot is 6 spaces past 2.11 (2.110): 2.116.

items.q: What number is halfway between 2.45 and 2.46?
items.e: 2.45 = 2.450 and 2.46 = 2.460. Halfway between 450 and 460 thousandths is 455: 2.455.

items.q: On a number line, which number is closest to 1?
items.e: Find how far each is from 1: 0.05, 0.1, 0.091 and 0.41. The smallest gap is 0.05, so 0.95 is closest.

items.q: Jack ran 3 710 km. Write this distance as a decimal.
items.e: 3 whole kilometres and 7 tenths: 3.7 km. 3.07 would be 3 and 7 hundredths.

items.q: Isla’s water bottle holds 0.75 L. Write this as a fraction of a litre.
items.e: 0.75 has two decimal places, so it is hundredths: 0.75 L = 75100 L.

items.q: The school rain gauge showed 15.4 mm on Monday, 9.8 mm on Tuesday, 15.2 mm on Wednesday and 4.6 mm on Thursday. Which day had the most rain?
items.e: Compare the whole numbers first: 15 > 9 > 4. Then 15.4 > 15.2 (4 tenths > 2 tenths). So Monday had the most rain.

items.q: At the athletics carnival, the long jump results are: Oliver 3.05 m, Kai 3.5 m, Leo 3.15 m and Noah 3.4 m. Who jumped the furthest?
items.e: Write them with 2 places: 3.05, 3.50, 3.15, 3.40. The greatest is 3.50 m, so Kai jumped furthest.

items.q: Grace is 1.4 m tall. Her brother is 1.39 m tall. Who is taller?
items.e: 1.4 = 1.40. Compare the tenths: 4 > 3. So 1.40 m > 1.39 m and Grace is taller.

items.q: Chloe swam 50 m in 40.5 seconds. Mei swam 50 m in 40.50 seconds. Who was faster?
items.e: 40.5 = 40.50, because a 0 at the end does not change the value. So they tied.

items.q: Lachlan swam 50 m freestyle in 41.27 seconds. What is the value of the digit 7?
items.e: 41.27: the 7 is the second digit after the point, so it is 7 hundredths of a second (0.07 s).

items.q: Sienna cuts four pieces of ribbon: 1.5 m, 1.455 m, 1.05 m and 1.505 m. Which piece is the longest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 1.500, 1.455, 1.050, 1.505. The greatest is 1.505 m, 5 thousandths longer than 1.5 m.

items.q: Mum buys 0.375 kg of cheese, 0.4 kg of ham, 0.35 kg of salami and 0.25 kg of olives. Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.375, 0.400, 0.350, 0.250. The greatest is 0.400 kg: the ham.

items.q: A builder has two boards. One is 1.205 m long and the other is 1.25 m long. Which board is longer?
items.e: 1.25 = 1.250. Compare the hundredths: 5 > 0. So 1.250 > 1.205 and the 1.25 m board is longer.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, the 50 m backstroke times are: Mia 42.5 s, Zara 42.45 s, Ruby 42.54 s and Matilda 42.6 s. The fastest time wins. Who won?
items.e: The fastest swimmer has the smallest time. Write them with 2 places: 42.50, 42.45, 42.54, 42.60. The smallest is 42.45 s, so Zara won. 42.5 is not less than 42.45.

items.q: Cooper’s time was between 39.8 s and 39.9 s. Which time could it be?
items.e: 39.8 = 39.80 and 39.9 = 39.90. Only 39.85 s is between them.

items.q: The rain gauge showed 23.4 mm. Write this as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 23 whole millimetres and 4 tenths: 23.4 mm = 23 410 mm.

items.q: In a 50 m freestyle race the times are: Cooper 39.9 s, Ethan 39.09 s, William 39.19 s and Liam 40.01 s. Who came second?
items.e: Smallest time first: 39.09 (Ethan), 39.19 (William), 39.90 (Cooper), 40.01 (Liam). So William came second.

items.q: The discus results at the athletics carnival are 12.08 m, 12.8 m and 12.18 m. Order them from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Write them with 2 places: 12.08, 12.80, 12.18. Greatest first: 12.8, 12.18, 12.08.

items.q: Four parcels have masses of 2.4 kg, 2.375 kg, 2.09 kg and 2.5 kg. Order them from lightest to heaviest.
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 2.400, 2.375, 2.090, 2.500. Lightest first: 2.09, 2.375, 2.4, 2.5.

items.q: Ava marks a measuring tape (in metres) with a red dot. What length does the dot show?
items.e: From 1.2 m to 1.3 m there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 0.01 m. Count 7 spaces on from 1.20: 1.27 m.

items.q: Mei measures a screw. It is 0.045 m long. Write this as a fraction of a metre.
items.e: 0.045 has three decimal places, so it is thousandths: 0.045 m = 451000 m (45 mm). 45100 m would be 0.45 m.

items.q: The winning time in a race was 35.2 seconds. Which time is 1 tenth of a second slower?
items.e: A slower time is a greater number. 35.2 + 0.1 = 35.3 s. 35.21 is only 1 hundredth more, and 35.1 s would be faster.

items.q: A koala sleeps about 0.8 of a day. Write 0.8 as a fraction in tenths.
items.e: 0.8 has one decimal place, so it is tenths: 0.8 = 810. Koalas sleep for most of the day.
